newsitem.title: NORWAY: Cruise liner passengers in Arctic to be evacuated.
newsitem.headline: Cruise liner passengers in Arctic to be evacuated.

text.p: The German owner of a cruise liner stranded off the Norwegian Arctic island of Spitzbergen said on Wednesday the 145 passengers would be evacuated because it was unclear when the ship could be pulled free.
Hamburg-based Hapag-Lloyd AG said the evacuation from the Hanseatic, a 9,000-deadweight-tonne luxury liner, would take place on Thursday by helicopter to a Norwegian coast guard ship.
Under the evacuation plan, the elderly passengers will be lowered to a huge flat icefloe at the stern of the ship.
"The icefloe is big enough for small helicopters to land and pick up passengers," Elisabeth Aarsaether, spokeswoman for the governor's office at Longyear, told the national news agency NTB.
The Bahamian-registered liner ran aground on a sandbank on Sunday in the Hinlopen fjord off Spitzbergen's north coast. It was on its way from Norway to Iceland via the rugged island.
Efforts to pull the Hanseatic off the sandbank have been hampered by drifting ice blocking rescue vessels from coming near her.
Hapag-Lloyd said it was unclear when the Hanseatic, which has a crew of 115, could be freed. "It will depend on the weather," the tour operator said in a statement.
As a result, the passengers would be taken off.

"The passengers will be transferred in the morning of July 17 by helicopter to the Nordkap, a Norwegian coast guard ship. The Nordkap will sail to the Longyear harbour, which it should reach before midnight," Hapag-Lloyd said.
"The guests will then take a charter flight to Hamburg, where they will arrive at 6 a.m. (on Friday). The guests, crew and ship are not in danger," it said.
Aarsaether said Norway had suggested that the passengers be evacuated while the weather was good and because they were elderly, with an average age around 70.
Coastguards planned to unload at least part of the ship's 480-tonne cargo of heavy fuel oil before attempting to drag her free.
Three rescue vessels involved in the operation were forced to pull out of the area on Tuesday to avoid getting trapped by the ice themselves.
